sections.overview: Apistogramma urteagai is a Peruvian dwarf cichlid described by Sven O. Kullander in 1986. Its type locality is Lake Túpac Amaru near Puerto Maldonado, in the Madre de Dios drainage. The species honours Peruvian biologist Jorge Andrés Urteaga Cavero, who helped lead the collecting expedition.
sections.identification: The narrow, strongly pigmented lateral band reaches the seventh bar but stops before the tail, leaving a separate caudal spot. A dark midventral stripe, short dorsal-fin lappets and rounded caudal fin complete the pattern. FishBase lists a maximum of 41 mm standard length for a male or specimen of unspecified sex; it gives no female-specific maximum, body mass, width or height. This helps distinguish it from Apistogramma resticulosa, whose band usually ends at bar six, and Apistogramma linkei, whose band and caudal spot join into a tail-shaped patch.
sections.habitat: Near Puerto Maldonado in Peru's Madre de Dios basin, it occurs along muddy lake margins, among pebbles in quiet streams, in swamps, and near vegetated stream mouths.
sections.diet: FishBase lists no prey records and gives only a trophic estimate inferred from close relatives, so there is no reliable species-specific prey list to report.
sections.behavior: A German keeper account describes it as a quiet, cover-seeking fish rather than an active open-water swimmer.
sections.reproduction: The female attaches eggs to the roof of a cave and tends the eggs and larvae.
sections.ecology: Kullander placed it in the Apistogramma regani group and noted its resemblance to Apistogramma resticulosa and Apistogramma linkei, while leaving their exact relationships unresolved.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment lists Apistogramma urteagai as Least Concern, assessed on 25 April 2014.
